subject: Model fit evals — open vs proprietary parity follow-up
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stein <alex.stein@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — open vs proprietary parity testing

Alex — great talking earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary from today's call:
- Objective: Validate whether open-source model variants can reach parity with your current proprietary baseline (PayGrid-Prod-v3) on user-facing generation quality while meeting latency and cost targets.
- Key acceptance criteria (from your PM/Eng notes): intent accuracy >= 95% on the core flows; mean response latency < 350ms p50 for typical queries; no high-severity hallucination regressions on the 200-case safety prompt set.

Redwood recommended evaluation plan:
1) Run parity evals on these candidates: r2-open-1.5 (quantized), r2-open-2.7 (FP16), and r2-llama-7B-optimized.
2) Benchmarks to capture: intent accuracy, slot-filling F1, top-1 output agreement vs PayGrid-Prod-v3, latency distribution, token-cost estimate.
3) Use your provided prompt set (attached: paygrid_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) and our benchmark template (attached) so we compute the same metrics.
4) Safety/quality regression check: we run the regression tests and highlight any clusters where open models diverge >5% on precision or introduce hallucinations above your tolerance.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Redwood will run an initial parity sweep on a 5k-sample subset (your choice) and deliver a report within 5 business days after you confirm the dataset.
- If parity looks promising, we'll run a full 50k evaluation and propose quantization/serving knobs to meet your latency targets.

Ask for PayGrid:
- Please confirm which dataset you'd like us to use (5k subset or full 50k).
- Confirm that we can run the proprietary baseline (we can accept a hashed/obfuscated export or run against an internal endpoint — whichever you prefer).

Links & attachments:
- Benchmark doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2B-paygrid-eval
- Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v2.jsonl, paygrid_benchmark_template.xlsx

Next step: once you confirm dataset, we’ll schedule the parity sweep and share an internal kickoff doc.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Stein <alex.stein@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — open vs proprietary parity testing

Thanks Lauren — helpful recap. Two quick clarifications: 

1) Parity definition: our internal team defines parity as (a) no more than 2% delta in intent accuracy vs PayGrid-Prod-v3; and (b) equal or better user-facing error rate on the top-10 flows. Is that consistent with Redwood’s approach?

2) Baseline access: we can give you an obfuscated export for the 50k test set (hashed ids + prompts + gold outputs). Are you able to run the proprietary baseline on your side if we provide a runbook/export, or do you need us to host an endpoint you can call?

We'd like the 5k sweep first. If it looks good we'll greenlight the full run. Also curious about quantization impact — historically we've seen regressions on slot-filling after aggressive 4-bit quant. Can Redwood measure that specifically?

—Alex
Alex Stein
Senior Product Manager, PayGrid
alex.stein@paygrid.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — open vs proprietary parity testing (internal)

Lauren / Aditya — quick internal note with details we should propose back to Alex.

Proposed technical approach (short):
- Candidate models: r2-open-1.5-q4_0 (4-bit quantized), r2-open-2.7-fp16, r2-llama-7b-optimized. We should also include r2-open-3.5-std if they want a higher-capacity point for comparison.
- Baseline handling: we can accept an obfuscated export. We'll run the PayGrid-Prod-v3 baseline as a black-box where we compare outputs and compute agreement/accuracy. If they provide an internal endpoint, we can call it (need auth token + rate limits).
- Metrics to compute: intent accuracy, slot F1, exact-match for critical fields, top-k agreement, BLEU/ROUGE not sufficient on its own so weight human-eval candidates where disagreement is high.
- Quantization/regression checks: run the eval across model variants and include a delta table showing per-flow regressions. Flag any flow with >5% drop in F1 or introduction of hallucination cases.

Operational notes:
- Sample sizes: do 5k sweep (stratified by flow), then 50k run if greenlit.
- Runtime: 5k sweep should be ~24 hours on dedicated infra with batching; include latency profile.
- Deliverables: CSV of outputs, metric dashboard link, and a short human-eval on 200 edge cases focusing on safety/hallucination.

Aditya — can you pre-allocate a small eval cluster (2xA10s or equivalent) and upload the metric script (we have one in /evals/parity-run) so we can turn this around in 5 business days? Also we'll prepare the human-eval rubric.

-Marissa
Director, Model Eval | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stein <alex.stein@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — open vs proprietary parity testing

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the 5k sweep. Quick answers and next steps below.

On parity definition: we understand PayGrid's parity target (<=2% delta on intent accuracy + no worse on top-10 flows). That's compatible with our evaluation framing — we'll report both absolute metrics and delta vs baseline.

On baseline execution: obfuscated export is fine. If you prefer, we can also call an internal endpoint — either works. For the export option we'll need hash-consistent ids + gold outputs and a short runbook for any context-window handling.

On quantization/regressions: yes — we'll measure slot-level F1 by flow and specifically include a quantization-impact matrix (4-bit vs 16-bit). We'll flag any flow with >5% F1 drop or hallucination spike.

Plan & immediate asks from PayGrid:
- Confirm: upload the 5k obfuscated export to the Drive folder (we'll share a write link) or provide endpoint creds.
- Confirm: any flows to exclude for privacy/PII reasons.

What we’ll deliver after the 5k run (timeline ~5 business days):
- Parity summary report (high-level verdict: pass/needs further tuning), detailed per-flow metrics, and a short list of recommended model & quantization configs to meet latency/cost targets.
- If pass: proposed rollout options (canary + fallback to PayGrid-Prod-v3) and an estimated cost delta.

I’ll drop a write link to the Drive folder and a HubSpot activity after this message.

Thanks — we’ll get the eval cluster provisioned and ping you once the run starts.

Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
